newsitem.title: UK: LME copper off highs by close, spreads still tight.
newsitem.headline: LME copper off highs by close, spreads still tight.

text.p: Copper was the major feature of London Metal Exchange (LME) trading up to Tuesday's close as tight nearby spreads flared on speculative short covering.
The all important cash to three months backwardation was last indicated at $240/$250, against Monday's late levels of around $175.
Earlier, tomorrow/next day traded at $20, just $3 under the LME limit of $23. On Monday, margin payments on spread business were doubled to $150 per tonne due to the market tightness.
Three months copper earlier rallied to a six-month high of $2,285 before drifting back to $2,258, up $54 from Monday.

Traders said they expected market conditions to remain choppy near-term. Open interest on $2,600 copper December calls will feature as the closer three months delivery gets to the $2,600 level, the more covering will have to be done.
Copper also found support from a warehouse stock fall of 3,850 tonnes to 6-1/4 year lows of 90,050 tonnes.
Traders are now expecting the market to consolidate before launching an attack on $2,300.
Other metals remained relatively quiet but found support from the uptrending copper market.
Aluminium moved towards $1,540 resistance and was last at $1,535, a gain of $22.
Nickel after earlier commission house selling bounced back with copper to $7,065, against $6,940.
